thread:
sandeep: FYI PineCard support pinged. They see ~30% throughput drop since the 199.3 deploy (~04:10 UTC). Can someone pick this up? https://support.example/ticket/PC-489
support-bot: Ticket PC-489 created, customer logs attached.
lucy: I'll take initial triage. Can you paste the customer config (model, batch_size, qps)?
adrian: Assigned. running benchmark now against the dedicated pool they use (dc-us-west-2:dedicated-43).
adrian: quick note — deploy at 04:10 touched kernel selector fallback logic and batching heuristics.
jorge: any traces? p99/inflight queue lengths?
adrian: here's a short sample from staging perf-run:
```
# perf harness run
model: redwood-v2-small
seq: 512
clients: 50
qps: 180
p50: 32ms
p95: 480ms
p99: 1.8s
throughput: 120 tok/s/node
```
keiko: that p99 is bad. Is this customer on KV cache? Could be cache invalidation regressing.
lucy: support-bot attached customer logs; searching for 'enqueue_ms' spikes.
support-bot: logs: https://s3.company/pc-489/logs.tar.gz
adrian: I see the kernel-selector falling back to slower kernels on node-12. Adding flamegraph and perf counters.
adrian: Ran `perf top` — top was soft-float path in attention kernel. suspect quantized path selection mismatch.
jorge: If kernel selector picks slower kernels for >512 seqs it could reduce per-GPU throughput. Any change in compilation flags in last deploy?
sandeep: last deploy toggled LD_PRELOAD for cuda-ops and bumped jemalloc; release note: 'kernel-selector: prefer stable kernels for mixed-sequence workloads'
keiko: can we reproduce quickly with a short A/B? adrian -> can you spin canary with prior kernel-selector?
adrian: spinning canary now: `deploy --image=runtime:199.1-prev --pool=dedicated-43 --tag=canary-pc489`
lucy: pinging PineCard support to schedule low-impact test window.
support-bot: Customer agreed to test at 16:00 PST
adrian: canary up. quick perf-run against same params:
```
qps: 180
p50: 30ms
p95: 160ms
p99: 210ms
throughput: 170 tok/s/node
```
Big improvement.
keiko: confirms regression tied to selector change. next steps: rollback to previous selector for dedicated-43 and open rollout pause until fix.
sandeep: +1. Please document RCA in postmortems channel and flag for release-blocker.
lucy: created follow-up ticket: RTE-742 — revert selector and add unit test for kernel preference on mixed sequences. cc @adrian @keiko
adrian: reverted canary to prev across pool. watching metrics.
ops-bot: autoscaling metrics show throughput recovering. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Customer notified; they confirmed observed improvement. Closing PC-489 on their side.
lucy: thanks team. I'll write a short summary for the customer and drop into #postmortems.
